title: E-bike-assisted exercise intervention to reduce cancer-related fatigue in breast cancer patients during radiotherapy
summary:
Cancer-related fatigue is one of the most common and debilitating side effects of breast cancer therapy (1)
and is associated with a significant reduction in quality of life (2). At the same time, therapy often leads
to reduced physical activity (3) and diminishing confidence in one's own physical capabilities,
which can create an additional barrier to exercise.
Although physical activity is recommended based on evidence as an effective measure for reducing fatigue (4)
and improving quality of life (5), its implementation in routine clinical practice is often hindered by
physical limitations and a lack of easily accessible programs. Furthermore, confidence in one's own
physical capabilities may decline during the course of therapy, causing patients to increasingly avoid
potentially beneficial activity.
In this context, the use of electrically assisted bicycles (e-bikes) represents an innovative,
practical, and accessible approach that allows for individually tailored exertion management
and makes physical activity feasible even during intensive phases of therapy. At the same time,
the daily commute to radiation therapy can be utilized actively and integrated into the
therapeutic routine as a valuable resource.

interventions.name:
Intervention group: Provision of an e-bike for the
daily commute to therapy as well as for optional use during
leisure time.
Control group: Standard transport; does not receive an e-bike.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Planned adjuvant radiotherapy
• Ability to ride a bicycle
• Ability to understand and complete questionnaires
• Written informed consent
• Place of residence within 20 km of the MHH
Exclusion criteria:
• Medical contraindications to physical activity
• Relevant mobility limitations
• Unsafe cycling ability
• Elite athletes
• Place of residence relative to MHH (distance of more than 20 km)
